found: the version "okhttp" of the catalog libs is 4.+: the prefix version 4.+ takes the newest version that starts with 4. when the build runs, so two builds of the same commit can use different versions
fix: write the one version the build should use, such as 4.12.0, and change it on purpose when you update; if a range is needed, lock the resolved versions with Gradle dependency locking

fix: add the key to [versions], or point version.ref at the key that holds the version

found: the library "core-ktx" of the catalog libs has the coordinates androidx.core:core-ktx, as the library "androidx-core-ktx" of the catalog libs does (examples/messy/gradle/libs.versions.toml:18); a build file can use either alias

found: androidx.core:core-ktx has version 1.12.0 in the library "core-ktx" of the catalog libs, and version.ref "coreKtx" (1.13.1) in the library "androidx-core-ktx" of the catalog libs (examples/messy/gradle/libs.versions.toml:18); which one the build gets depends on resolution

found: jcenter() is a repository of this build, and JCenter is read-only and takes no new versions; a dependency that is only there cannot be updated, and Gradle deprecates jcenter()
